name: Transnational feminism
summary: Transnational feminism is a critical feminist paradigm and activist network that analyses how globalization, capitalism, colonial legacies and the nation-state shape women's lives across borders. It rejects a universal 'global sisterhood' modelled on Western women's experience in favour of solidarity built across differences of race, class, nation and sexuality. It opposes neoliberal globalization, imperial and 'humanitarian' wars, and restrictive migration regimes, while still using rights and international law to protect women.
scope: The academic and activist current from Grewal and Kaplan's Scattered Hegemonies (1994), Alexander and Mohanty's Feminist Genealogies, Colonial Legacies, Democratic Futures (1997) and Mohanty's 'Under Western Eyes' and Feminism Without Borders, plus networks such as AWID, DAWN and WLUML. Most of the test (institutions, technology, defence detail) lies outside what this literature addresses, so many answers are low-confidence inferences from its anti-capitalist, anti-imperial and intersectional principles.

keyFigures.name: Chandra Talpade Mohanty
keyFigures.role: Author of 'Under Western Eyes' and Feminism Without Borders; leading theorist of the paradigm.

keyFigures.name: Inderpal Grewal
keyFigures.role: Co-coined the theory with Caren Kaplan in Scattered Hegemonies (1994).

keyFigures.name: M. Jacqui Alexander
keyFigures.role: Co-editor with Mohanty of Feminist Genealogies, Colonial Legacies, Democratic Futures (1997).

sources.title: Transnational feminism
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Definition, thinkers, positions on capitalism, empire, migration, veil, human rights, war and networks.

sources.title: Feminist Perspectives on Globalization
sources.author: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy
sources.usedFor: Structural adjustment, care chains, sex work, rights, nation-state, war, unions, global justice.

sources.title: Under Western Eyes: Feminist Scholarship and Colonial Discourses
sources.author: Chandra Talpade Mohanty
sources.usedFor: Critique of the universal 'Third World woman', universal patriarchy, religion, family, imperialism and capital.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Feminist critiques of structural adjustment stress cuts to public services that push care work onto women, so public provision of health care is favoured.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Mohanty is described as anti-capitalist, and neoliberal markets are held to exploit Third World women, so market superiority is rejected.

unions-good.rationale: Labour unions are listed among the anti-globalization networks that can support North-South women's coalitions.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Transnational feminists hold that corporations and global capital reach across borders and harm women workers, calling for constraint of corporate power.

cut-welfare.rationale: Feminist analysis of structural adjustment treats cuts to public services as harming women and shifting burdens onto them.

strong-leader.rationale: Opposition to hierarchy and concentrated power and emphasis on grassroots solidarity make a strong leader bypassing gridlock unattractive.

state-harmful.rationale: The state is criticised as a limiting framework, but transnational feminists also demand state and international action on women's rights, so full anti-statism is not held.

empower-police-military.rationale: Feminists link militarism to neoliberalism and oppose war; expanding military authority runs against this.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: The SEP notes sex work rose under structural adjustment and does not take a side; transnational feminists are split between labour-rights and anti-trafficking views.

decide-locally.rationale: Value local grassroots groups, yet stress that local conditions are shaped by transnational forces that national or local units cannot handle alone.

traditional-family.rationale: Mohanty rejects treating the patriarchal family as a universal oppressor, yet the movement does not endorse traditional family structure as society's foundation.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Intersectional approach includes sexuality; support for legal recognition is the mainstream view though local variation exists.

abortion-legal.rationale: Reproductive autonomy is a standard feminist position; transnational feminism stresses context but supports women's control over their bodies.

more-religion-public.rationale: Mohanty warns against reducing women to religion, but also resists Western secularist caricatures; no wish for a larger public role is stated.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: The paradigm centres race and colonial legacies and calls for addressing their continuing oppression.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Gender is analysed as constructed through colonial, economic and cultural relations, not as a natural given.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Transnational feminism rejects nation-bound frameworks and critiques nationalist appeals that often police women.

gradual-change.rationale: Activist and critical paradigm aiming at structural transformation rather than respect for established institutions.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Migrants, especially women of colour, are framed as bearing the burden of global capitalism; restricting migration is opposed.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Support for transnational governance and networks, but strong criticism of UN and rights bodies as Western-centred; split.

free-trade.rationale: Neoliberal trade and globalization are held to harm Third World women; Mohanty is explicitly against capitalist globalization.

nation-first.rationale: The "transnational" label was chosen to reject nation-state-centred frames and promote cross-border solidarity.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Transnational feminists oppose "humanitarian" wars fought in women's name, citing Afghanistan and Iraq as imperialist.

open-borders.rationale: Opposes restrictive migration regimes that endanger migrant workers, though SEP notes no explicit open-borders endorsement.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Climate change is treated as a border-crossing, gendered harm requiring collective action.

revolution-justified.rationale: Mohanty calls for anticapitalist struggle but sources do not endorse or reject revolution; adherents are split.

experts-over-public.rationale: Core critique is of Western experts and academics claiming to speak for Third World women; local and subaltern voices are prioritised.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Critique of free trade, but protectionism by nation-states runs against transnational framing; split.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Not a stated aim; transnational feminism seeks fair pay and recognition of labour rather than abolishing wages.

one-party-rule.rationale: Opposes hegemonic structures and emphasises grassroots and plural voices, so single-party leadership is rejected.

democracy-best.rationale: Mohanty co-edited work on democratic futures and feminists push for women's representation in governance.

war-builds-character.rationale: Militarism is criticised and war-related sexual violence stressed as a serious crime.

separate-church-state.rationale: Mohanty refuses to equate religion with oppression and rejects Western secularist framing; adherents split.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Laws like Pakistan's Zina ordinances are criticised as oppressive to women.

military-superiority.rationale: Imperial military dominance is criticised as hegemonic.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Mohanty attends to class but explicitly rejects reducing oppression to a single economic cause.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Seeks wider rights for women, and warns against community norms that subordinate them.

restore-past-order.rationale: Seeks structural transformation of existing hierarchies, not restoration of past order.

direct-action.rationale: An activist movement built around grassroots organizing and transnational networks.

means-match-ends.rationale: Stresses solidarity and non-hierarchical practice that reflect the world sought.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Mohanty stresses exploitative economic exchange and the harm of global capitalism to women workers.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Mohanty describes contemporary imperialism as supported by monopoly and finance capital.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Critiques liberal rights frameworks as tied to Western individualism and the nation-state, and looks to collective and social-economic rights.

positive-liberty.rationale: Social and economic rights and material conditions for agency are core demands.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Imperialism is the central object of critique.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Mohanty argues Western feminist knowledge production is a power-laden discourse of colonization.

universal-morality.rationale: Rejects ethnocentric universalism, though seeks cross-border solidarity and normative standards.

single-common-good.rationale: Emphasises differences and conflicts of power among women and groups rather than one common good.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Labour power and women's bargaining power are central concerns.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Austerity-style fiscal restraint is criticised for burdening women.

economic-freedom.rationale: Neoliberal "economic freedom" is criticised as harming women.

national-self-determination.rationale: Anti-colonial sympathy for self-determination, but critical of nation-state framework.

force-without-un.rationale: Opposes unilateral imperial wars such as Iraq.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Mohanty warns against reducing religion to a cause or imposing secular Western reason; no endorsement of reason-only.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Migrants are central concerns; excluding them from welfare conflicts with solidarity.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Care work is undervalued; compulsory work requirements are opposed as punitive.

dominated-front.rationale: Anti-imperial but wary of nationalist blocs; split.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Opposes laws that assign distinct gender roles.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Opposes cultural-homogenizing demands on migrants, particularly women of colour.

national-mission.rationale: Criticises Western impositions of political models as hegemonic.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Core premise; patriarchal structures are analysed alongside capital and colonialism, though Mohanty rejects a single universal patriarchy.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Accountability for war-related sexual violence is endorsed (Rome Statute).

night-watchman-state.rationale: Rejects minimal-state libertarianism in favour of social and economic rights.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Opposes racism. The sources are silent on it.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Women's rights as human rights; equality across nations and races is central.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Mohanty cautions against both Western and religious absolutes; split.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Calls for democratic futures and inclusion of marginalized women's voices.

population-transfer.rationale: Opposes forced displacement and ethnic nationalism.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Opposition to domination in all forms (patriarchal, imperial, capitalist) closely matches this view.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Concern for poor and marginalized women, especially in the Global South, is central.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Labour organizing is supported as a vehicle for women's coalitions.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Poverty is attributed to economic structures and imperial relations, not population.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Celebrates difference and rejects this claim.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Post-9/11 wars and security measures are criticised.

party-commands-army.rationale: Authoritarian arrangement incompatible with the movement's anti-militarism.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Migrants' rights are central; barriers to citizenship are opposed.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Supports transnational governance beyond Westphalian states, but criticises EU-style neoliberal institutions.

clerical-rule.rationale: Clerical rule that restricts women conflicts with feminist aims.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Opposes imperial wars but sources do not endorse revolutionary defeatism.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Moral censorship often targets women; opposed.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Academic scholarship is the movement's own home though it self-critiques; this populist claim is rejected.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Mohanty rejects hierarchies placing Western feminism or culture above others, but does not endorse relativism of all practices.

death-penalty.rationale: Opposed to state violence; no support for execution.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Feminists split on pornography and the sources take no side.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Mohanty warns against both Western and religious absolutes; split.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Debt and structural adjustment programs are criticised for feminizing poverty.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Political independence without economic transformation leaves imperial relations intact; Mohanty ties imperialism to capital.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Growth-first developmentalism is criticised for harming women.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Global justice duties are discussed, though aid-based paternalism is criticised.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Anti-militarist. The sources are silent on it.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Opposes imperial occupation, citing Iraq and Afghanistan.

character-from-environment.rationale: Gender and identity are seen as socially constructed.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Punishing leaving religion conflicts with autonomy.

women-must-cover.rationale: Opposes coerced dress codes, though also opposes bans.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Mohanty stresses economic relations but warns against reducing everything to a single cause.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Minority and women's rights need protection from majorities.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Women's underrepresentation in governance is a central concern.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Feminist global justice literature supports binding labour standards in trade.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Critiques Western-centred knowledge; wants plural histories.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The "civilizing" rhetoric is the core target of the colonial discourse critique.

patriotic-education.rationale: Nationalism is rejected as a frame.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Mohanty stresses differences in women's positions across the world, but not this specific thesis.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Opposes discrimination. The sources are silent on it.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Rights frameworks are criticised as Western and state-bound, yet rights protection is used.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Charity-based paternalism is rejected in favour of rights and structural justice.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: An activist movement that treats political engagement as essential.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Mohanty analyses how Western feminist discourse secures hegemony through knowledge production and representation, not only force.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Mohanty describes imperialism as sustained by monopoly and finance capital and exploitative economic exchange between North and South.

native-born-offices.rationale: Opposes citizenship hierarchies that exclude migrants from public life.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Irredentist demands conflict with the rejection of nationalism and anti-militarism.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Colonial and racial histories are taken seriously.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Anti-militarist. The sources are silent on it.

paid-care-work.rationale: Care work and global care chains are central; a global right to care is proposed.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Women's autonomy within marriage is a standard feminist position.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Privatization of social provision is criticised.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Intersectional analysis focuses on structural effects over intent.

corporate-influence.rationale: Concern with corporate and capitalist power over governance is central.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Transnational networks and NGOs rely on cross-border funding.

non-intervention.rationale: Opposes imperial wars, but supports transnational action on rights and sexual violence, so absolute non-intervention is not held.

informal-organisation.rationale: Networks are used but formal NGOs are also a major channel.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Rejects nation-state primacy; uses international instruments such as the Rome Statute.

defeat-communism.rationale: Cold-war anti-communism is not part of the movement.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Anti-capitalist. The sources are silent on it.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Women's oppression is tied to global capitalism and economic structures; central anticapitalist argument in Mohanty.

socialized-care.rationale: Care ethics literature supports public provision of care, though adherents also highlight need for recognition.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Nationalism and cultural purity are rejected.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Anti-capitalist but not aligned with a third way.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Opposed to denialism. The sources are silent on it.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Opposes blasphemy laws. The sources are silent on it.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Imperialism criticised. The sources are silent on it.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Grassroots participation by marginalized women is central.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Transnational intersectionality extends the framework of interlocking oppressions with global forces, as the Wikipedia article states.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Intersectional inclusion of gender and sexuality.

alienated-labor.rationale: Anti-capitalist critique of exploitative labour for women.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Rejects essentialising Islam as monolithic; Mohanty criticises such reductions.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Not accepted. The sources are silent on it.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Bans on religious dress impose Euro-patriarchal notions, per the Wikipedia article.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Structural adjustment programmes are attacked as feminizing labour and burdening women.

property-franchise.rationale: Opposes exclusion. The sources are silent on it.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Environmental harms to women are noted; eco-feminist linkage endorsed by many.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Islamic feminism appears as a variant; reinterpretation is an accepted route.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Anti-capitalist concern with concentrated global capital.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Supports public provision and rights over charity.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Women's equality across institutions; Islamic feminism is cited.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Anti-militarist. The sources are silent on it.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: US military presence is linked to harms, as with Pakistan.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Anticapitalist. The sources are silent on it.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Mohanty argues that 'women' cannot be assumed a coherent group with shared oppression across contexts, and the Wikipedia article reports the rejection of shared experience.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Privatization of water and services criticised.

family-wage.rationale: Male breadwinner model is criticised by feminists.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Intersectional, cross-cutting coalitions favoured over racial-bloc organising.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Mohanty rejects a unified category of women; yet care ethics valued.

arms-reduction.rationale: Anti-militarist. The sources are silent on it.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Global capitalism is condemned; transforming international economic rules is a core aim.

sacred-nation.rationale: Rejects nationalism. The sources are silent on it.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Rejects ahistorical universals yet seeks solidarity.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Anti-militarist. The sources are silent on it.

ban-fgm.rationale: Mohanty critiques Western framing but local women's activism opposes FGM; most adherents support prohibition.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Calls for substantive democratic futures beyond procedure.

premarital-sex.rationale: Opposes Zina laws, per the Wikipedia article.

women-suffrage.rationale: Transnational feminists still use rights and international law to protect women, so equal political rights are taken as a baseline even though the literature stresses more than formal rights.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Mohanty criticises Western feminist portrayals of Third World women, especially Muslim women, as oppressed mainly by religion; oppression is located in colonial, economic and state structures.

race-social-construct.rationale: The paradigm analyses race as produced by colonial and capitalist histories and treats it as a category of power, not a natural division.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: The paradigm criticises colonial legacies and nation-state borders but also seeks stability for women; adherents have no documented position.

simple-living.rationale: The literature criticises consumer capitalism but does not hold simple self-sufficient living as an ideal.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Adherents are split between opposing settler colonialism and opposing restrictive migration regimes, which the paradigm criticises.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Transnational feminism defends human rights and criticises punitive state violence, so killing without trial is rejected.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Networks such as WLUML campaign for equal family-law rights including women's access to divorce.

national-resource-control.rationale: It opposes foreign corporate extraction but also distrusts nation-state control; adherents are split.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: The paradigm centres race and colonial legacies as structural obstacles, so the claim is rejected.

material-over-identity.rationale: Intersectional, difference-centred analysis insists identity and material issues cannot be separated.

missingStatements.text: Feminist solidarity should be built across differences between women rather than on the assumption of a shared global female experience.
missingStatements.rationale: The paradigm replaced 'global sisterhood' with solidarity across difference, and Mohanty rejects assuming women are a coherent group.

missingStatements.text: Western military interventions justified as liberating women do more harm than good.
missingStatements.rationale: Transnational feminists oppose 'humanitarian' wars fought in women's name, citing Afghanistan and Iraq.

notes: Strands differ on sex work, on rights language (Western-centred versus a tool of 'globalization from below') and on the veil. Many 'not addressed' answers are inferences from anti-capitalist, anti-imperial and intersectional principles and are low confidence.
